title: How Iran war is driving Turkey’s defense deals with Qatar, Gulf states
author: Barin Kayaoglu
text:
Analysis

How Iran war is driving Turkey’s defense deals with Qatar, Gulf states

The Iran war has created new urgency for Turkey and its Gulf partners to strengthen defense ties, giving Ankara an opening to court investment and expand markets for its defense industry.

Barin Kayaoglu

Turkish commandos perform a drill during a Teknofest Blue Homeland event at the Naval Command on Aug. 21, 2026, in Golcuk, Turkey. — Burak Kara/Getty Images

ANKARA — Turkey's flurry of defense agreements with Gulf and Asian partners is pursuing two goals: closer military coordination as the Iran war spills across the region, and foreign investment to sustain its expanding defense industry.On Nov. 13, Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defense agreement, the latest in a series of deals Ankara has struck in recent months to deepen military and defense industry ties. The pact follows an October memorandum of understanding, "Badr," signed by Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia to expand defense industry cooperation through joint production, research and development. Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan also signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement on Aug. 7, committing to treat an armed attack on any one of the signatories as an attack on all three.Turkey has maintained a military presence in Qatar since 2015 under a 2014 defense agreement between the two countries. Ankara expanded its troop presence in June 2017, shortly after Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Egypt severed diplomatic ties with Doha over its regional policies and ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, which the four countries designate as a terrorist organization.
